name: Soil Moisture
description: The moisture content of the soil significantly affects the robot's traction and speed on both paths. Path 2 (grass) will be much more dramatically affected by changes in moisture (e.g., due to recent rain) compared to Path 1 (track). This creates distinct travel time groups.

name: Track Condition (Path 1)
description: The quality of the track surface – smoothness, presence of debris, compaction – will heavily influence travel time. Variable track conditions will lead to distinct travel time groups.  This is likely the strongest driver of the multimodal distribution for Path 1.

name: Grass Density (Path 2)
description: The density of the grass on Path 2 will change seasonally and with varying growth. Denser grass will slow the robot down more significantly than sparse grass. This creates a major variability in travel times.

name: Weather - Rain/Wetness
description: Rain dramatically impacts both paths. Path 2 (grass) is much more sensitive, leading to slower speeds and increased travel times.  Even a light drizzle can cause significant deviations in time.

name: Weather - Wind
description: Wind can affect the robot's stability, especially when navigating Path 2, and could cause deviations in its course. Strong winds could also create a need for the robot to choose a different, more sheltered route even if that wasn't the optimal one.

name: Time of Day (Solar Position)
description: The position of the sun affects the lighting conditions and can influence camera accuracy, potentially leading to slight deviations in navigation. Path 2 is more vulnerable to this due to less consistent lighting.

name: Robot Speed Settings
description: The robot's controller may have a speed setting. Variations in this setting will affect the travel time for both paths. The choice of speed may vary based on Path condition.

name: Grass Type
description: The type of grass on Path 2 (e.g., Rye, Fescue) will have different physical properties that affect its resistance to the robot's wheels and therefore its travel speed.

name: Debris on Path 2
description: Small stones, twigs, or other debris on Path 2 can cause the robot to slow down or even stall.

name: Slope/Terrain
description: Even subtle slopes on either path will impact travel time. Path 2, with its uneven surface, will be more sensitive.

name: Robot Battery Level
description: As battery level decreases, the robot’s speed may be reduced, introducing variability into travel times.

name: Track Surface Temperature
description: The temperature of the track surface can affect tire grip and therefore travel speed. This is particularly relevant with changes in weather.

name: Grass Height
description: The height of the grass on Path 2 will directly affect the robot’s ability to navigate, and is correlated with grass density

name: Robot Localization Accuracy
description: Errors in the robot’s localization (where it thinks it is) could lead to deviations in its path and therefore in travel time.  Especially true with visual odometry.

name: Robot Wheel Slip
description: The degree to which the robot’s wheels slip during movement will affect its speed and travel time. This is correlated with soil moisture, track conditions and speed settings.
